title: Member Accounting Memo: Billing Error Corrections and the Date Arrears Moved Into a Payment Arrangement
content:
**Member accounting memo — Payment Arrangements (Deferred Payment Agreements): when the corrected line was billed**

**Rule.** Billing error correction credits of the latest bill that are applied at a default count further according to when the corrected line was billed:

- in full where the corrected line was billed on or before the day the balance was moved into the agreement, its overbilled amount having been moved in with the arrears;
- at 50 percent (0.5) of their amount where it was billed after that day;
- not at all where no correction credit was posted on the latest bill.

**Records read.** The *corrected line* is the bill line on the member's Electric Service by Rate Schedule account that the latest billing error correction credit of the latest bill refers back to, taken at its bill date. *The day the balance was moved into the agreement* is the date of the balance-transfer entry on the agreement's ledger. The *latest bill* is the bill of the latest installment's billing period on the agreement.

| Corrected line billed | Correction credit counts |
|---|---|
| before the day of the balance transfer | in full |
| on the day of the balance transfer | in full |
| the day after the balance transfer or later | 50 percent |
| no correction credit on the latest bill | not at all |

**Hypothetical:** balance moved into the agreement on March 4. A correction credit of $32.00 on the latest bill for a usage line billed February 20 counts as $32.00; for a line billed April 3 it counts as $16.00.
